subject: Upfront commitment: invoicing entity, FX & tax routing
messages:
From: Olga Garcia <ola.garcia@globea.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Anders Holm <a.holm@globea.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at Globea is preparing a standard upfront commitment (prepay) for our AI tooling spend and we have a few tax / billing questions before we proceed to SOW and PO. High level: we are evaluating a 2-year prepay with a modest ramp in year 1 and would like clarity on invoicing entity options, VAT treatment, FX exposure, and potential withholding tax (local WHT).

Specifics:
- Globea is an EU legal entity (Belgium). We prefer EUR invoicing if possible.
- We need to understand if Redwood can invoice from a European entity to avoid WHT and ease VAT handling.
- If Redwood invoices from the US, will Globea be required to withhold taxes? If so, is Redwood willing to provide a gross-up or WHT certificate?
- Any precedent for VAT reverse-charge or local VAT registration?
- Also curious how you handle FX on multi-year prepay (fixed USD contract vs. monthly FX conversion).

Can you share sample invoicing options and a proposed ramp/discount schedule for 1/2/3-year prepay commitments? We need this for our legal and tax team review before issuing an LOI.

Appreciate a short call if helpful.

Best,
Olga
Procurement, Globea Inc.
[Globea PO contact: procurement@globea.com]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Olga Garcia <ola.garcia@globea.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Hi Olga — thanks, and great to hear Globea is moving toward a prepay.

Quick note: looping in Marissa (sales lead), Ava (finance) and Priyom (legal) so we can propose safe options for EU customers. I can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow if helpful.

Next steps I will take now:
- Share two invoicing approaches (US invoicing w/ WHT annex vs EU invoicing via Redwood Luxembourg)
- Draft a simple ramp + discount schedule for 12/24/36-month prepay commitments
- Flag FX handling options (invoice currency vs monthly conversion) and WHT treatment for each approach

Will follow up with a short note this week and attach a pricing worksheet and draft SOW.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-options-2026.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Team — quick internally-facing note before we respond to Globea:  

Options we usually offer for EU enterprise prepay: 
1) Invoice from Redwood Luxembourg (or EU entity) in EUR — minimizes WHT exposure and supports standard EU VAT treatment. Customer gets a single invoice in EUR, VAT reverse-charge possible if customer is VAT-registered. Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with local entity rules.

2) Invoice from Redwood US in USD — simpler for us operationally, but Globea would likely need to withhold local tax (Belgium WHT can apply depending on service classification). We can offer a WHT annex and provide certificates where available. For material WHT we typically negotiate a gross-up in contract in larger deals.

FX handling:
- Preferred: invoice in customer currency when invoicing via Luxembourg.
- Alternate: invoice in USD and apply a monthly FX conversion using close-of-business FX rate on invoice date — but customer pushback is common.

Term / prepay economics (draft):
- 12-month prepay: no term discount, small onboarding credit if >$100k
- 24-month prepay: 2% term discount on committed spend (front-loaded credits), 12-month ramp (50% year 1 usage credit availability, full in year 2)
- 36-month prepay: 4% term discount, 24-month ramp schedule

Legal: Priyom — can you call out any material compliance or tax risks with option (1) vs (2)? If Luxembourg invoicing requires a permanent establishment or registration, flag that. Also confirm typical WHT mitigations / required docs.

—Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:10:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Marissa / team — short legal/tax note: 

- Luxembourg invoicing is our standard approach for EMEA where we can avoid customer-side WHT and support local VAT mechanics (reverse-charge) — provided we do not create a PE and the contract is managed from our EU commercial desk. Finance (Ava) please confirm whether we can book revenue to LU entity for Globea scale.
- If we invoice from the US, Globea may be required to withhold (typically 0–15% depending on treaty). To address: we can provide a WHT annex and certificate of tax residency; gross-up is negotiable but should be limited to material amounts — recommend we aim for no gross-up but accept a modest carve for first-year only if necessary.
- FX: Recommend customer-currency invoices for term deals; if USD invoice required, include a defined FX conversion method and cap (e.g., monthly spot rate with +/- 2% collar) to limit volatility disputes.

I can draft a one-page WHT annex and a short invoicing appendix for the SOW. Jonas — tell Globea we can outline both paths and recommend LU invoicing as preferred for EU customers.

Priyom

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Olga Garcia <ola.garcia@globea.com>
Cc: Anders Holm <a.holm@globea.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Hi Olga / Anders — thanks for the clear list of questions. After internal review we can offer two practical paths for Globea: 

Option A — EU invoicing (recommended)
- Invoice through Redwood Luxembourg in EUR. VAT: reverse-charge if Globea is VAT-registered (we will capture VAT IDs). No WHT expected.
- Term economics: 24-month prepay — 2% term discount applied to committed USD-equivalent; ramp: 50% credit available in Y1, full credit in Y2.
- FX: invoice fixed in EUR (no monthly revaluation).

Option B — US invoicing (if preferred)
- Invoice from Redwood US in USD. Globea would be responsible for any WHT. We will provide a WHT annex and certificate of residence; we are open to negotiating a 1-year limited gross-up in the event material WHT (>5%) is applied.
- Term economics: same discount schedule but we invoice in USD; FX conversion will use the invoice date spot rate (we can add a +/-2% collar).

Attachments: redwood-pricing-options-2026.xlsx (pricing scenarios), draft-sow-globea.pdf (SOW template), wht-annex-template.pdf (WHT annex).

If you confirm preference (Option A vs B) we will prepare a short invoicing appendix and update the SOW for sign-off. Happy to take a 30-min call — propose Thu 15 Apr 09:00 CET / 08:00 GMT.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Anders Holm <a.holm@globea.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Olga Garcia <ola.garcia@globea.com>, procurement@globea.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Jonas — thanks for the options and the documents. Globea preference is Option A (EU invoicing) if Redwood can issue invoices from a European entity (Luxembourg would be fine). Two quick clarifications: 

1) We will need invoices in EUR, net of any WHT. Please confirm Louvre/RD entity details so our accounts payable can route payments.
2) For the ramp: can you make the Y1 credit availability 60% instead of 50%? Our consumption is expected to ramp faster in the first 9 months.

If LU invoicing is available and you accept the 60% Y1 ramp, we should be able to proceed to a PO this month.

Regards,
Anders
Head of Procurement, Globea Inc.
[procurement@globea.com]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Anders Holm <a.holm@globea.com>, Olga Garcia <ola.garcia@globea.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Upfront commitment — invoicing & international tax questions

Anders / Olga — good news: finance confirms we can route Globea through Redwood Luxembourg and issue EUR invoices. We also agreed to the adjusted ramp. Summary for SOW / PO: 

- Invoicing entity: Redwood S.à r.l. (Luxembourg) — billing in EUR, VAT rules apply (reverse-charge where valid). I will share entity details in the invoicing appendix.
- Term: 24-month prepay, 2% term discount on committed spend.
- Ramp: 60% of committed credits available in year 1, 100% in year 2.
- WHT: not expected under EU invoicing; if any local tax arises we will address via the WHT annex, but this should not be required for LU invoices.
- FX: invoices fixed in EUR for the term.

Next steps: I will attach an updated SOW and the invoicing appendix for your AP team, together with the WHT annex as a precaution. Please confirm and we will push the PO path.

Attachments: draft-sow-globea.pdf, wht-annex-template.pdf

Thanks everyone — happy to jump on a quick call if any final items.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft-sow-globea.pdf]
